# Existence and unipotence of groups generated by root subsets

Module `Langlands.GroupScheme.Rational.RootSubsetGroupExistenceProof`.
Namespace `Langlands.GroupScheme`. Universe parameter `u`.

## Result and provenance

The theorem `rootSubsetGroupExistence` has exactly the type
`RootSubsetGroupExistenceStatement.{u}`, imported from
[`ClosedRootSubsetStatements`](ClosedRootSubsetStatements.md).
It proves the existence assertion implicit in Renard V.4.2's notation
`G(X)` and `U(X)`, including unipotence of `U(X)` for unipotent root subsets.
The published statement's Markdown gives the source comparison with Renard,
*Représentations des groupes réductifs p-adiques*, French edition dated
9 July 2026, V.4.2 (printed p.118 / PDF p.124), and Borel–Tits,
*Groupes réductifs* (1965), §3.8. This module is a derived proof from the
published Library results listed below; its implemented route uses the Weyl
action on cocharacters and dynamic unipotent subgroups.

Let `k : Type u` be any field, `G` a connected reductive group scheme over
`Spec k`, and `i : T.toGrp ⟶ G` a maximal split torus.

For every `X ⊆ relativeRoots i`, the theorem constructs both:

- a closed subgroup `h : H ⟶ G` satisfying `IsRootSubsetGroup i X h`,
  with `H` smooth, affine and connected;
- a closed subgroup satisfying `IsRootSubsetUnipotentGroup i X h`,
  again with smooth, affine, connected source.

The first subgroup contains the torus centralizer and every root subgroup
indexed by `X`; the second contains just those root subgroups. Each is minimal
among all closed subgroups containing its generators, with containment understood
as inclusion of subgroup functors on every test scheme.

For either ambient root set allowed by `IsRelativeRootAmbient i R`, a generic
cocharacter `ν`, and `IsUnipotentRootSubset i ν R X`, the theorem also proves
`IsUnipotent H` for every closed representative `h : H ⟶ G` satisfying
`IsRootSubsetUnipotentGroup i X h`. Here `IsUnipotent` is the published
representation-theoretic predicate: every nonzero finite-dimensional
representation has a nonzero fixed vector.

## Passing from represented functors to generated groups

The private lemma `exists_smooth_generated_functors` packages
`FiniteGeneration.exists_smooth_generated_family` for a family of subgroup
functors `F : I → SubgroupFunctor G`. Its hypotheses require `G` to be smooth
and affine and each `F a` to satisfy `RelativeRoot.IsSmoothConnectedClosed`.
The latter supplies a smooth connected closed representative of each functor;
the representative is affine because it is closed in the affine ambient group.

The proof chooses these representatives and applies the published generated
family theorem. The equality between each representative's range and `F a`,
together with `factorsThrough_hom_iff_range_le`, converts the resulting
factorization conditions into inclusions of subgroup functors. The same
conversion in the other direction proves minimality against an arbitrary
closed subgroup `q : K ⟶ G`. No smoothness or connectedness assumption is
imposed on this competitor `K`.

This helper is an internal reformulation of the published generation theorem.
It returns the closed generated representative, inclusion of every generator,
minimality, and smoothness, affineness and connectedness of its source.

## Constructing `G(X)` and `U(X)`

The connected reductive hypothesis supplies smoothness and affineness of `G`
and connectedness of its underlying space. The maximal split torus hypothesis
supplies `IsSplitTorus T.toGrp`, a closed torus inclusion and its monomorphism
instance.

Every `a ∈ X` is a nonzero character, since `X ⊆ relativeRoots i`.
`RelativeRoot.subgroup_isSmoothConnectedClosed_of_ne_zero` therefore supplies
the required smooth connected closed representative of
`RelativeRoot.subgroup i a`.

For the centralizer, `torusCentralizer_hasSmoothClosedRepresentative` supplies
a smooth closed representative `z : Z ⟶ G` of `torusCentralizer i`.
`IsSplitTorus.connectedSpace_centralizer` supplies connectedness of `Z`.

To construct `G(X)`, apply the helper to the family indexed by `Option X`:
`none` denotes the torus centralizer, and `some a` denotes the root subgroup
for `a.val`. Its containment and minimality conclusions are precisely the
conjuncts of `IsRootSubsetGroup`.

For `U(X)`, apply the helper to the root subgroups alone, indexed by `X`.
Its conclusions give `IsRootSubsetUnipotentGroup`. The construction works for
every subset of the relative roots, including the empty subset.

## Unipotence

From `IsUnipotentRootSubset i ν R X`, choose `w` with
`X ⊆ relativeWeylCharacterAction i w '' positiveRootSubset R ν`.
Set

```text
ζ = relativeWeylCocharacterAction i w ν,
χ = CommGroupScheme.groupHom ζ ≫ i.
```

For each `a ∈ X`, write `a = w b` with `⟨b, ν⟩ > 0`. The published pairing
invariance theorem `latticePairing_relativeWeyl` gives
`⟨a, ζ⟩ = ⟨b, ν⟩ > 0`. Then
`RelativeRoot.subgroup_le_dynamicUnipotent` puts every generating root
subgroup inside `Dynamic.unipotent χ`, on all test schemes.

Let `j : U ⟶ G` be the closed affine representative supplied by
`Dynamic.Affine.unipotentScheme` and `Dynamic.Affine.unipotentHom`.
Its representation and closedness theorems identify its range with
`Dynamic.unipotent χ`. Its source is smooth by `dynamicSmooth`, hence locally
of finite type. For any `h : H ⟶ G` as in the unipotence conclusion,
the minimality in `IsRootSubsetUnipotentGroup i X h` gives
`range h ≤ range j`.

The representation's `factorHom` constructs `f : H ⟶ U` with `f ≫ j = h`.
`IsClosedSubgroup.of_comp` makes `f` a closed immersion because `h` and `j`
are closed immersions. Finally, `dynamicUnipotentUnipotence` proves
`IsUnipotent U`, and `unipotentClosedSubgroup` gives `IsUnipotent H`.
Thus this conclusion applies to every representative satisfying the
specified minimality, without requiring that it be the representative
chosen in the existence construction.

The positivity argument uses the Weyl-image condition directly, so it works
uniformly for both permitted ambient root sets. It does not need closedness of
`X` or genericity beyond the hypotheses already carried by the target.
